Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

18:1544-1973 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
COTTON CALICO 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 30 March 1973, after the draft finalized by the 
Cotton and Cotton Products Sectional Committee had been approved by 
the Textile Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was originally published in 1960. This revision is 
based on IND/TC/0040 (c) * Calico, Cotton*, issued by the Ministry of 
Defence, Government of India. 

03 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2- 
1960^. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value 
should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes construcdonal details and other partici lars 
of cotton calico, bleached or dyed used for the borders of mo6quito nets, 
and in the fabrication of ground sheets. 

1.2 This standard does not specify the general appearance, feel» shade, 
etc, of the doth. 

2. MANUFACTURE 

2.1 Yam — Cotton yam used in the manufacture of the cloth shall be 
satisfactory in evenness and reasonably free from neps and spinning defects. 

2J Cloth — The cloth shall be bleached or dyed as required. The 
bleached cloth shall have a fully bleached finish free from any blueing or 
optical whitening agents. 

NoTB — The desired whiteness of the cloth should be achieved only by impert* 
inf full blenched finish free from any blueing/whitening agents, if desired by the 
buyer. 



^Rnles for rounding off numerical values ( rensid). 

3 



I8slS44-»7S 

2*2.1 The cloth shall be dyed to suiublc shades as agitbed to between 
the buyer and the seller. The dyeing shall be free fimn streaks and 
stains. 

2.2.2 The cloth shall be free from dressing and filling materials and bom 
substances liable to cause subsequent tendering. 

2.2 J The cloth, when visually examined, shall be reasonably free from 
spinning, weaving and pr3ces$ing defects. 

3. REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 Conatrocdoii — The cloth shall comply with the requirements 
specified in Table 1 excepting count of warp and weft which have been 
given only for guidance. 

3.2 ColcNir Faatnesa — The colour fastness shall comply with the require- 
ments specified in Table 2. 

33 Other rcqiiiremi^nts of the cloth shall be as given in Table 3. 

4. MARKING 

4.1 The cloth shall be marked with the following: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Width and length of the piece; 

c) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark, if any; and 

d) Year of manufacture. 

4.1.1 The cloth may also be marked with the Standard Mark* 

NOTE — The use of the Standard Msrlc is governed by the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 sod the Rules snd Regulations made there- 
under. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that 
sundard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control 
which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked produas are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may 
be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

4.2 At the other end of the piece, the cloth shall be marked with an 
identification mark. 

5. PACKING 

5.1 The cloth shall be packed in bales or cases in conformity with the 
procedures laid down m IS: 1347-1972* or in IS:293-1967t, as required.

C. SAMPLING 

€•1 For determining the conformity in respect of the physical character- 
isticts namely* ends and picks, weight per square metre^ breaking load, 
width and length, the scale of sampling and the criteria for conformity as 
given in IS: 3919-1966* shall be followed. 

6.2 For ascertaining the conformity in respect of scouring loss, ^H value, 
shrinkage or elongation, colour fastness and estimation of iron, copper and 
maitganese metals, the scale of sampling and criteria for conformity as 
given in IS : 5463-19691 shall be followed.
